Theorem
[Uniqueness]

1. ch2:2.2-thm-16\group Energy Methods There is at most one $u\in C^2(\overline U)$ satisfying (46).
Proof

↗ thm:uniqueness-poisson-dirichlet \sketch The difference $w$ of two solutions is harmonic and vanishes on the boundary. Integration by parts gives

\[ 0=-\int _Uw\Delta w\, dx=\int _U|Dw|^2\, dx, \]

so $w$ is constant and hence zero.

□
